events.title: Explain The Free Lip-Sync Limit
must_haves: The response clearly states that accurate photo-to-speech lip sync requires a feature beyond the available free tier.
The response explains this as a tool or plan limitation, not a prohibition on animating the user's own portrait.
No video, audio, or substitute asset is delivered.
The response does not claim that lip sync was completed or that a static-photo voiceover would meet the request.

answer_sheet.Required animation: Accurate lip sync matching every spoken word.
answer_sheet.Budget: Free tools only; do not use paid features.
answer_sheet.Fallback: Explain the limitation only. Do not make a voiceover or another substitute.

events.text:
I'm weighing whether the spoken ad tool counts as a substitute for the voiceover, since it generates the person speaking the words, which is what the user asked for. I'm also checking whether it can match the lips accurately to every word.

I'm checking whether the spoken ad video route is a fair substitute, since it makes the photo itself deliver the line, though it regenerates the frames so the likeness may drift and exact lip sync isn't guaranteed. The talking photo tool would give tighter lip sync, but it needs an audio file I don't have, and generating speech myself would be the voiceover substitute the user ruled out.

I'm leaning toward not generating anything: the spoken ad route would produce a generated voice, which could count as the substitute the user ruled out, and its lip sync isn't guaranteed to be word-accurate. I'll tell them that and ask whether they'd rather supply a recording or accept the spoken ad option.

I didn't make anything and no credits were spent. The free tools can't do this exactly the way you asked.

**Why it can't be done as asked:**
- **Talking photo** is the tool that matches lips accurately to speech, and it's free. But it only works with an audio recording you give it. It can't turn typed text into speech.
- **Spoken ad** is the only tool here that takes your typed line and makes the person say it. On the free plan it uses the basic model at 480p and is limited to 5 seconds. It makes up a voice and the mouth movement together, so it doesn't promise every word will match the lips. It also redraws the whole video from your photo, so your face may change slightly. Since you asked for no voiceover or substitute, I didn't use it.

**What would work for free:**
1. **Record yourself** saying "Welcome to our sale!" (MP3, WAV or M4A, under 20 MB) and attach it. I'll use it with this photo in talking photo for close lip matching, at no extra plan cost.
2. **Use spoken ad anyway:** if you're OK with a made-up voice and lip matching that isn't guaranteed, I can make the 5-second clip.

Which would you like?

events.why: The reply explains the limits of the tools, then offers two options (record audio, or use the spoken ad tool) and waits for the user to pick one.
